enzyme_name: carotenoid glucosyltransferase CruC plus an unidentified carotenoid-glucoside acyltransferase
organism_context: Thermus thermophilus HB27
rationale: Thermocryptoxanthin-13 is beta-cryptoxanthin first glucosylated (by the megaplasmid glycosyltransferase CruC, whose deletion leaves the carotenoid unglucosylated) and then esterified with a C13 fatty acid by an acyltransferase that has never been identified. No single enzyme catalyses this entry, so functionality cannot be assigned.
direction_note: Both collapsed steps are biosynthetic group transfers onto the carotenoid, so flux runs beta-cryptoxanthin -> thermocryptoxanthin (left-to-right); MSDB also records a C19/H34/O6 mass imbalance because the glucosyl and acyl donors are absent.

enzyme_name: zeaxanthin glucosyltransferase CruC plus an unidentified carotenoid-glucoside acyltransferase
organism_context: Thermus thermophilus HB27
rationale: Thermozeaxanthin-13 is zeaxanthin glucoside esterified with a C13 fatty acid; CruC was shown to be the glycosyltransferase (the delta-cruC mutant accumulates free zeaxanthin), but the acyltransferase performing the second step is unidentified, so this entry has no single catalyst.
direction_note: Glucosylation and acylation both run biosynthetically (zeaxanthin -> thermozeaxanthin, left-to-right); the entry is also mass-unbalanced by C19/H34/O6 since both donors are missing.

enzyme_name: zeaxanthin glucosyltransferase CruC plus an unidentified carotenoid-glucoside acyltransferase
organism_context: Thermus thermophilus HB27
rationale: Same chemistry as the other thermozeaxanthins, differing only in the C15 acyl chain: CruC glucosylates zeaxanthin and a still-unidentified acyltransferase esterifies the glucose, so no one enzyme runs the entry as written.
direction_note: Biosynthetic direction is zeaxanthin -> thermozeaxanthin-15 (left-to-right); MSDB flags a C21/H38/O6 mass imbalance from the absent glucosyl and acyl donors.

enzyme_name: zeaxanthin glucosyltransferase CruC plus an unidentified carotenoid-glucoside acyltransferase
organism_context: Thermus thermophilus HB27
rationale: Zeaxanthin -> thermozeaxanthin-17 again lumps CruC-catalysed glucosylation with esterification by an uncharacterised acyltransferase; the catalysing protein for the acyl step is unknown.
direction_note: Direction is biosynthetic left-to-right; the C23/H42/O6 mass imbalance means the reported deltaG (and hence ModelSEED's reverse call) describes an impossible transformation.

enzyme_name: carotenoid glucosyltransferase CruC plus an unidentified carotenoid-glucoside acyltransferase
organism_context: Thermus thermophilus HB27
rationale: Thermobiszeaxanthin-13-13 is thermozeaxanthin-13 carrying a second glucosyl-acyl unit on the other ionone ring, so the entry again collapses a glycosyl transfer (CruC) and an acyl transfer (enzyme unidentified) into one step.
direction_note: Elaboration of the carotenoid runs left-to-right; the stripped equation is mass-unbalanced by C19/H34/O6.

enzyme_name: carotenoid glucosyltransferase CruC plus an unidentified carotenoid-glucoside acyltransferase
organism_context: Thermus thermophilus HB27
rationale: Second-ring glucosylation plus acylation of thermozeaxanthin-15 to thermobiszeaxanthin-13-15; CruC covers the glycosylation but the acyltransferase remains unidentified, so no single enzyme catalyses the entry.
direction_note: Biosynthetic direction is left-to-right; MSDB records a C19/H34/O6 mass imbalance.

enzyme_name: carotenoid glucosyltransferase CruC plus an unidentified carotenoid-glucoside acyltransferase
organism_context: Thermus thermophilus HB27
rationale: Thermozeaxanthin-17 to thermobiszeaxanthin-15-15 again lumps glucosylation and acylation; only the glycosyltransferase (CruC) is known, and the acyl-chain bookkeeping in the ModelSEED pair is itself inconsistent (C17 ester mapped onto a 15-15 bis-ester).
direction_note: Direction is biosynthetic left-to-right; the entry is mass-unbalanced by C19/H34/O6 so no thermodynamic direction is meaningful.

enzyme_name: dehydrosqualene synthase (CrtM)
organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus; squalene-synthase (SQS/CrtM) fold
rationale: CrtM is one squalene-synthase-fold polypeptide that condenses two farnesyl diphosphates head-to-head and rearranges the presqualene-diphosphate intermediate to dehydrosqualene without releasing it, which is a single catalytic activity rather than two. Its broad chain-length promiscuity is substrate tolerance, not a second activity.
direction_note: The real reaction is 2 FPP -> dehydrosqualene + 2 PPi and is made irreversible by diphosphate loss; ModelSEED kept only one FPP and no PPi (status MI:C:15/H:22/O:-7/P:-2, CI:2), destroying that driving force and with it the basis for the reverse call.

enzyme_name: glycosyl-4,4'-diaponeurosporenoate acyltransferase (CrtO)
organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus crtOPQMN operon; note the unrelated CrtO beta-carotene ketolase of cyanobacteria/mycobacteria is a different protein
rationale: KEGG assigns R07656 to CrtO (K10212), the acyltransferase that esterifies glucosyl-4,4'-diaponeurosporenoate with 12-methyltetradecanoate to give staphyloxanthin; it is a single acyltransferase and the five other pathway activities sit on separate proteins (CrtM, CrtN, CrtP, CrtQ, AldH).
direction_note: KEGG itself labels R07656 'incomplete reaction' because the activated acyl donor is omitted (MSDB status MI:C:15/H:28/O:1); acyl transfer from a thioester is irreversible toward staphyloxanthin, i.e. left-to-right.

enzyme_name: not identified - an O2-dependent aromatic ring-hydroxylating dioxygenase, or a cytochrome P450 acting with a separate epoxide hydrolase
organism_context: PAH-degrading actinobacteria (e.g. Mycobacterium vanbaalenii PYR-1) attack anthracene at both C1,2 and C9,10
rationale: ModelSEED gives only EC 1.14.-.- with no xref, and anthracene 9,10-oxidation is run either by a multicomponent ring-hydroxylating dioxygenase (separate oxygenase/ferredoxin/reductase polypeptides, which is a complex and not a fused enzyme) or by a P450 plus a distinct epoxide hydrolase; the entry does not say which, so the catalysing protein is genuinely unidentified.
direction_note: The real reaction consumes O2 and NAD(P)H, which is what makes anthracene -> dihydrodiol one-way; MSDB's water-only equation is charge-imbalanced by 2 (a hidden 2-electron oxidation) and so loses the driving force that would otherwise settle the direction.

enzyme_name: none identified - apparently spontaneous intramolecular lactonization of the anthracene ring-fission product
organism_context: anthracene-degrading Mycobacterium sp. PYR-1 cultures
rationale: KEGG R07693 carries no EC and no orthology and is annotated both 'unclear reaction' and 'incomplete reaction'; 6,7-benzocoumarin is recovered as a dead-end cyclization product alongside the anthracene ring-fission acid rather than as the product of any named enzyme.
direction_note: Lactonization to the aromatic coumarin is effectively irreversible left-to-right, but the entry also loses a CHO2 fragment (MSDB MI:C:-1/H:-1/O:-2, CI:1), so no deltaG-based direction for it is meaningful.

enzyme_name: 2-hydroxylaminobenzoate mutase (NbaB)
organism_context: Pseudomonas fluorescens KU-7 2-nitrobenzoate catabolism; 35% identical to the 4-hydroxylaminobenzoate lyases (PnbB)
rationale: NbaB is a 181-residue single-activity mutase that performs the intramolecular hydroxyl transfer converting 2-hydroxylaminobenzoate to 3-hydroxyanthranilate; no second catalytic activity is reported for it, and the upstream nitroreductase NbaA is a separate protein.
direction_note: The mutase is a committed catabolic step toward 3-hydroxyanthranilate (left-to-right); the entry is mass- and charge-balanced, so ModelSEED's reverse recommendation is not excused by an equation defect.

enzyme_name: isoflavone 7-O-glucoside beta-glucosidase (isoflavone conjugate-hydrolysing beta-glucosidase, ICHG; glycoside hydrolase family 1)
organism_context: legumes - Medicago truncatula, soybean (apoplastic GmICHG), guar
rationale: KEGG annotates R07733 as the 'isoflavone glucoside glucosidase' step, i.e. hydrolysis of ononin to formononetin, and the characterised legume ICHGs are single-active-site family-1 beta-glucosidases with no second catalytic function.
direction_note: The enzyme behind this entry is a hydrolase, so it runs ononin -> formononetin (left-to-right); the glucosylating direction ModelSEED recommends is a different enzyme (a UDP-glucose:isoflavone 7-O-glucosyltransferase) and a different reaction, and the glucose and water are missing here anyway (MI:C:-6/H:-11/O:-5).

enzyme_name: vestitone reductase (VR)
organism_context: Medicago sativa (alfalfa); isoflavone-reductase/PIP family, penultimate enzyme of medicarpin biosynthesis
rationale: KEGG R07737 is EC 1.1.1.348 vestitone reductase (K13265), an NADPH-dependent single-domain oxidoreductase that reduces the vestitone 4-keto group to give 7,2'-dihydroxy-4'-methoxyisoflavanol (DMI); the downstream DMI dehydratase is a separate protein.
direction_note: NADPH is what drives vestitone -> DMI; ModelSEED replaced NADPH/NADP+ with two bare protons (status CI:-2), removing the reductant that fixes the direction and leaving a near-zero deltaG that flips the call.

enzyme_name: pterocarpan reductase (PTR)
organism_context: Lotus japonicus / L. corniculatus; PIP (phenylcoumaran benzylic ether reductase) family
rationale: KEGG R07739 is pterocarpan reductase (K13266, EC 1.23.1.-), an NADPH-dependent reductase that cleaves the medicarpin dihydrofuran to the isoflavan (-)-vestitol; the four cloned Lotus PTRs are single-activity PIP-family reductases.
direction_note: Reductive ring opening is NADPH-driven and runs irreversibly toward vestitol (left-to-right); writing the hydride as two protons (status CI:-2) hides that and makes the step look reversible.

enzyme_name: isoflavonoid malonylglucoside malonylesterase (medicarpin 3-O-glucoside-6''-O-malonate esterase)
organism_context: legume vacuolar isoflavonoid conjugate turnover (Medicago truncatula)
rationale: KEGG annotates R07742 only as 'isoflavone malonylglucoside malonylesterase', with no EC and no orthology, and no protein performing this specific demalonylation has been cloned, so its domain architecture is unknown even though the chemistry is a plain ester hydrolysis.
direction_note: An esterase runs demalonylation (left-to-right); the malonylation direction ModelSEED recommends needs malonyl-CoA and a BAHD acyltransferase, and the malonyl group is simply absent here (MI:C:-3/H:-1/O:-3).

enzyme_name: pterocarpan 3-O-glucoside beta-glucosidase (isoflavonoid conjugate-hydrolysing beta-glucosidase, GH1)
organism_context: elicited legume tissue (Medicago truncatula) releasing the phytoalexin medicarpin from its stored glucoside
rationale: KEGG annotates R07743 as the 'isoflavone glucoside glucosidase' step - hydrolysis of medicocarpin to medicarpin - and all characterised legume enzymes of this class are single-active-site GH1 beta-glucosidases, but no medicocarpin-specific protein has been cloned, so the assignment is by class rather than by identified gene.
direction_note: Phytoalexin release runs glucoside -> aglycone (left-to-right); the reverse glucosylation is a separate UGT reaction needing UDP-glucose, and the glucosyl unit is missing from this equation (MI:C:-6/H:-10/O:-5).

enzyme_name: pterocarpan 3-O-glucoside beta-glucosidase (trifolirhizin beta-glucosidase, GH1)
organism_context: legumes storing maackiain as its 3-O-glucoside trifolirhizin (Trifolium, Sophora, Cicer)
rationale: KEGG annotates R07756 as the 'isoflavone glucoside glucosidase' step, hydrolysing trifolirhizin to the phytoalexin (-)-maackiain; family-1 beta-glucosidases of this type carry a single catalytic site, but no trifolirhizin-specific protein has been cloned so the call rests on the enzyme class.
direction_note: Hydrolytic release of maackiain runs left-to-right; the glucose and water are absent from the equation (MI:C:-6/H:-10/O:-5), so the deltaG behind ModelSEED's reverse call is not for this chemistry.

enzyme_name: cobalt-precorrin methyltransferase CbiE/CbiT (fused as CbiET; CobL in the aerobic route)
distinct_activities: cobalt-precorrin-7 C15-methyltransferase with C12 decarboxylation (CbiT module; EC 2.1.1.196)
organism_context: fused single chain as CbiET in Bacillus megaterium and as CobL in the aerobic Pseudomonas denitrificans pathway; separate CbiE and CbiT polypeptides in Salmonella enterica and Methanocaldococcus jannaschii
rationale: This step is run by the CbiE C5-methyltransferase module, which in B. megaterium (purified as CbiET) and in the aerobic CobL orthologue sits on the same polypeptide as the CbiT C15-methyltransferase/C12-decarboxylase module. Because CbiT itself carries both methyl-transfer and decarboxylation chemistry, some authors describe the fusion as trifunctional.
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH methylation is irreversible left-to-right, and the fusion channels the product straight into the adjacent methyltransferase module on the same chain; ModelSEED also dropped the CO2 that KEGG's balanced R07774 releases (status MI:C:-1/O:-2, CI:1).

enzyme_name: not identified
rationale: KEGG R07783 carries no EC, no orthology and the comment 'unclear reaction'; no protein has ever been assigned to the 3,5-dibromo-4-hydroxybenzoate / 2,6-dibromophenol interconversion, so there is no enzyme to classify.
direction_note: CO2 is missing from the equation (MI:C:-1/H:1/O:-2, CI:1), and 4-hydroxybenzoate (de)carboxylases of this family are used in vivo in both directions (phenol carboxylation in anaerobes, decarboxylation elsewhere), so the enzymology does not pick a side.

enzyme_name: cyclopropanecarboxyl-CoA ring-opening enzyme ('decyclase'), protein never purified
organism_context: Rhodococcus rhodochrous grown on cyclopropanecarboxylate as sole carbon source
rationale: Toraya et al. demonstrated an inducible activity in R. rhodochrous extracts that opens the cyclopropane ring of cyclopropanecarboxyl-CoA en route to crotonyl-CoA and 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA, but the protein was never purified or sequenced, so nothing is known about its domain content.
direction_note: Relief of cyclopropane ring strain plus the catabolic context (ring opening feeds straight into beta-oxidation) make cyclopropanecarboxyl-CoA -> crotonyl-CoA the physiological direction, i.e. left-to-right; the equation itself is balanced, so ModelSEED's reverse call has no equation defect to blame.

enzyme_name: none - non-enzymatic collapse of the FMO-generated thiobenzamide S,S-dioxide (a reactive sulfene)
organism_context: rat liver microsomes (flavin-containing monooxygenase); also seen in Ralstonia pickettii TA thioamide catabolism, where benzonitrile appears as an intermediate between thiobenzamide S-oxide and benzamide
rationale: Thiobenzamide is S-oxidised twice by the flavin-containing monooxygenase to the chemically reactive S,S-dioxide, which then breaks down without catalysis; KEGG R07838 accordingly has no EC, no orthology and the comment 'unclear reaction', so there is no enzyme to classify.
direction_note: A reactive sulfene collapsing to the nitrile is one-way chemistry (left-to-right), and the sulfur leaving group is simply absent from the equation (MI:H:-1/O:-2/S:-1), so the reverse is not even formulable.

enzyme_name: acyl-CoA oxidase (ACX1)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana peroxisomal beta-oxidation of OPC-8:0-CoA in jasmonate biosynthesis; ACX1/ACX5 are the long/medium-chain-preferring isoforms
rationale: KEGG assigns R07888 to EC 1.3.3.6 acyl-CoA oxidase (K00232), and plant ACXs are single-activity homodimeric flavoproteins; the multifunctional enzyme of this pathway (AIM1/MFP2, enoyl-CoA hydratase plus 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase) catalyses the next step, not this one.
direction_note: Acyl-CoA oxidase reoxidises its tightly bound FAD with O2 to H2O2, and it is that O2 coupling - not the flavin itself - which makes the dehydrogenation irreversible left-to-right; writing free FAD/FADH2 instead leaves a near-equilibrium deltaG that invites ModelSEED's reverse call.

enzyme_name: acyl-CoA oxidase (ACX1/ACX5 class)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana peroxisome, second beta-oxidation round of jasmonate biosynthesis (OPC-6:0-CoA)
rationale: Identical enzymology to the OPC8-CoA step but two carbons shorter: KEGG assigns R07892 to EC 1.3.3.6 acyl-CoA oxidase (K00232), a single-activity homodimeric flavoprotein, with the shorter chains handled by the medium-chain ACX isoforms.
direction_note: The irreversibility comes from O2-dependent reoxidation of the bound flavin to H2O2, which the free FAD/FADH2 formulation omits; the enzymatic direction is OPC6-CoA -> trans-2-enoyl-OPC6-CoA, left-to-right.

enzyme_name: acyl-CoA oxidase (ACX1/ACX5 class)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana peroxisome, third beta-oxidation round of jasmonate biosynthesis (OPC-4:0-CoA, the round that yields jasmonoyl-CoA)
rationale: KEGG assigns R07896 to EC 1.3.3.6 acyl-CoA oxidase (K00232); plant ACXs are single-activity homodimeric flavoproteins and the multifunctional AIM1/MFP2 protein acts only on the enoyl product of this step.
direction_note: O2-coupled flavin reoxidation to H2O2 is what drives the dehydrogenation forward (OPC4-CoA -> trans-2-enoyl-OPC4-CoA, left-to-right); the free FAD/FADH2 stand-in removes it.
